text: From the parts catalogue, place the servo, the extrusion, a pair of T-nuts and the bolts, with the servo's output shaft upright, and declare that layout.

The servo must go straight down into a pocket in the block, with 0.3 mm of clearance around the body on every side and 0.3 to 2.5 mm of space under its bottom, and its ears must rest on top of the block.
Four M4 bolts through the servo's four ear holes into pilot holes in the block hold it in place, and a screwdriver must be able to reach each one.
Keep the servo's cable exit, output spline and horn sweep clear of any printed material.

The block rests on a flange sitting flat on the extrusion, secured by two M5 bolts passing through clearance holes into T-nuts in the extrusion's top slot, along its centreline. The bolts sit 60 to 110 mm apart along the slot, with the servo's output spline between them in X. Each bolt must be long enough to engage its nut yet not reach the slot floor, and the flange must extend 3 mm or more around each bolt head.

Put one gusset on each side of the block, tying it to the flange. Each is 3 to 8 mm thick, at least 10 mm long along the flange and at least 15 mm high up the block. With both, the block-to-flange section must be at least 1.25 times as stiff in bending (second moment of area about the axis along the extrusion) as the block footprint alone.

The mount has to survive a 1.5 N m servo torque reaction. Spell out the load path from the servo through the M4 bolts, the block, the gussets and the flange to the two M5 extrusion bolts, and keep it inside the stress, bearing and bolt limits. Use this model and these limits. Thread shear in PLA is 4 MPa on the pilot cylinder; the tab-bolt thread strength must be at least 3 times the bolt shear, with the bolts sharing the torque according to how far each is from the centroid of the four holes. In the block-to-flange junction allow 2 MPa shear and 3 MPa bending. Under an M5 head allow 5 MPa bearing, and 500 N tension for each T-nut. The side force at the horn is the torque divided by a 25 mm horn reach; it acts across the extrusion at the mid-height of the horn plate and tips the mount about the extrusion's edge, which is 10 mm from the bolt line. The two M5 bolts carry it in proportion to their X distance from the spline.
With the M5 bolts slackened, the T-nuts and the mount should slide along the slot, and a screwdriver should reach every M5 bolt.
The mount must be a single manifold body that can be printed on an FDM printer with no supports.
The mount must not exceed 130 x 70 x 45 mm.

Deliverables are an STL in the assembly pose, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout, the load-path statement and the agent's own clearance report. The report and the statement must both agree with an independent measurement.
